Increasing demand for connected vehicles, advanced driver assistance systems, electric vehicles, and software-based automotive technologies is creating new opportunities for vehicle manufacturers and technology providers worldwide.

The Software-Defined Vehicles Market is experiencing significant transformation as automotive manufacturers shift from traditional hardware-focused vehicle development toward software-controlled vehicle platforms. Software-defined vehicles (SDVs) allow manufacturers to introduce new features, improve vehicle performance, enhance safety, and update digital systems without requiring major physical modifications.

The growing integration of artificial intelligence, cloud computing, vehicle connectivity, and over-the-air software updates is accelerating the adoption of software-defined vehicle technologies. Software-Defined Vehicles Market Overview

The Software-Defined Vehicles Market is becoming an important part of the global automotive industry's digital transformation. Modern vehicles increasingly depend on software to manage essential functions, including navigation, entertainment, battery management, vehicle diagnostics, driver assistance, and connected services.

Unlike conventional vehicles, which rely heavily on separate electronic control units, software-defined vehicles use more integrated computing systems and centralized software platforms. This approach helps automotive manufacturers reduce system complexity, improve software management, and introduce new vehicle capabilities throughout the product lifecycle.

Software-Defined Vehicles Market Growth Drivers

One of the major factors supporting Software-Defined Vehicles Market growth is the increasing adoption of connected automotive technologies. Consumers expect modern vehicles to provide smartphone integration, real-time navigation, digital entertainment, remote access, and advanced safety features.

The expansion of advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) is another important growth factor. Software-defined vehicle platforms support technologies such as adaptive cruise control, lane-keeping assistance, automated emergency braking, driver monitoring, and intelligent parking assistance. Automotive manufacturers are investing in artificial intelligence and machine learning to improve vehicle decision-making and support more advanced driving capabilities. These technologies process information from cameras, radar, sensors, and other vehicle systems to enhance driving safety and operational performance.

Over-the-air software updates are also transforming the automotive industry. Manufacturers can remotely introduce security improvements, fix software issues, and add selected vehicle features without requiring customers to visit service centers. Furthermore, the growing focus on electric mobility, digital vehicle services, and centralized automotive computing is encouraging partnerships between automobile manufacturers, semiconductor companies, cloud service providers, and software developers.

Software-Defined Vehicles Market Trends

The Software-Defined Vehicles Market is witnessing rapid technological changes as automotive companies introduce advanced software architectures and intelligent vehicle platforms. A major trend is the transition toward centralized and zonal computing architectures. These systems help manufacturers manage multiple vehicle functions through fewer, more powerful computing platforms, reducing dependence on numerous independent control units. Another important trend is the integration of artificial intelligence into automotive software. AI-powered systems support predictive maintenance, intelligent navigation, driver behavior analysis, and improved vehicle diagnostics.

Cybersecurity is becoming increasingly important as connected vehicles exchange information with external networks. Manufacturers are strengthening software security, data protection, and vehicle communication systems to reduce digital risks. The expansion of vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication is also attracting industry attention. This technology allows vehicles to exchange information with transportation infrastructure, other vehicles, and connected systems, supporting safer and more efficient mobility. Additionally, manufacturers are exploring subscription-based software features and digital services that can create ongoing revenue opportunities after the initial vehicle purchase.

Software-Defined Vehicles Market Segmentation Analysis

The Software-Defined Vehicles Market is segmented by vehicle type and application, reflecting the growing use of software technologies across different automotive platforms.

By Type

ICE Vehicles: Internal combustion engine vehicles are increasingly adopting software-defined technologies to improve engine management, vehicle connectivity, safety systems, and digital entertainment. Automotive manufacturers are introducing software-based functions into conventional vehicles to improve performance and customer experience.

Electric Vehicles: Electric vehicles represent an important opportunity for software-defined automotive development. Advanced software platforms support battery management, charging optimization, energy efficiency, vehicle connectivity, and intelligent powertrain operations. The expansion of electric mobility is encouraging investment in integrated vehicle software systems.

By Application

ADAS & Safety: Software-defined platforms support driver assistance, collision prevention, automated braking, lane monitoring, and other safety-related functions. Continuous software improvements help manufacturers enhance supported vehicle capabilities.

Connected Vehicle Services: Connected services include navigation, infotainment, remote vehicle monitoring, digital communication, and cloud-based automotive applications. These features are becoming important considerations for modern vehicle buyers.

Autonomous Driving: Software-defined systems provide the computing infrastructure needed to process sensor information, support driving decisions, and develop automated driving functions.

Body Control & Comfort System: Software technologies manage vehicle lighting, climate control, seating adjustments, access systems, and personalized comfort settings.

Powertrain System: Advanced software supports engine control, electric motor operation, energy management, transmission functions, and vehicle performance optimization.

Regional Insights into the Software-Defined Vehicles Market

North America: North America is an important market for software-defined vehicle innovation, supported by automotive technology companies, semiconductor developers, connected vehicle platforms, and investment in advanced driving systems. The United States plays a significant role in automotive software research and development.

Europe: Europe continues to advance software-defined automotive technologies through established vehicle manufacturers, automotive suppliers, and engineering companies. Germany is particularly important because of its automotive manufacturing base and investment in next-generation vehicle electronics.

Asia-Pacific: Asia-Pacific offers substantial opportunities for software-defined vehicle adoption because of its large automotive manufacturing industry, expanding electric vehicle ecosystem, and growing demand for connected transportation. China, Japan, South Korea, and India are important markets for automotive software development and digital mobility solutions.

Middle East & Africa: The Middle East and Africa present developing opportunities as automotive connectivity, electric mobility infrastructure, and intelligent transportation initiatives expand. Adoption is expected to develop alongside improvements in digital infrastructure and vehicle technology availability.

Competitive Landscape and Key Market Players

The Software-Defined Vehicles Market features competition among automotive manufacturers, semiconductor companies, software developers, and established automotive technology suppliers.

Key companies operating in the market include:

  • Robert Bosch GmbH
  • Nvidia Corporation
  • APTIV
  • Valeo
  • Marelli Holdings Co., Ltd.
  • Continental AG
  • Volkswagen Group
  • Tesla
  • HARMAN International

These companies contribute to the development of automotive computing platforms, embedded software, connected vehicle systems, driver assistance technologies, and advanced electronic architectures.

Nvidia Corporation develops accelerated computing technologies used in automotive AI and autonomous driving development. Robert Bosch GmbH provides automotive electronics, software solutions, and mobility technologies. APTIV focuses on vehicle architecture, connectivity, and advanced automotive systems.

Continental AG, Valeo, and Marelli contribute automotive electronics and software-related solutions, while Volkswagen Group and Tesla are involved in developing digitally integrated vehicle platforms. HARMAN International supports connected vehicle experiences, and BlackBerry Limited provides software technologies used in embedded automotive systems.

Competition is increasingly influenced by software capabilities, cybersecurity, system integration, computing performance, and the ability to deliver continuous vehicle improvements.

Investment Opportunities in the Software-Defined Vehicles Market

Growing investment in automotive digital transformation is creating opportunities across software engineering, semiconductor development, cloud infrastructure, cybersecurity, and intelligent vehicle platforms. Automotive manufacturers are allocating resources toward next-generation electrical and electronic architectures that can support multiple vehicle models and software applications. Standardized software platforms can help manufacturers improve development efficiency and manage vehicle functionality across different product lines.

The expansion of electric vehicles creates opportunities for companies developing battery management software, charging systems, digital diagnostics, and energy optimization technologies. Automotive cybersecurity also represents an important investment area. As vehicles become more connected, manufacturers require reliable solutions to protect vehicle networks, software updates, communication channels, and sensitive information.

Technology partnerships between automakers and software providers are expected to remain important as the industry develops more advanced and adaptable vehicle platforms.

Challenges Affecting Software-Defined Vehicles Market Expansion

Despite strong growth opportunities, software-defined vehicle development involves several challenges. One major concern is the complexity of integrating software and hardware systems from different suppliers. Manufacturers must ensure that vehicle components operate reliably across multiple computing platforms and software environments.

Cybersecurity threats present another challenge because connected vehicles rely on communication networks and software-based controls. Automotive companies must maintain secure systems throughout the vehicle lifecycle. High development costs, specialized engineering requirements, software testing, and regulatory compliance can also create difficulties for manufacturers. Additionally, maintaining software reliability is essential because vehicle systems directly influence safety and performance. Manufacturers must conduct extensive testing before introducing updates that affect critical vehicle functions. Addressing these challenges will be important for supporting wider adoption of software-defined automotive technologies.

Future Outlook of the Software-Defined Vehicles Market Through 2035

The future of the Software-Defined Vehicles Market is closely connected to the development of intelligent mobility, connected transportation, electric vehicles, and automotive artificial intelligence. As vehicle manufacturers introduce more advanced computing architectures, software is expected to control a growing number of automotive functions. Digital platforms will help manufacturers provide personalized driving experiences, improve vehicle maintenance, and introduce additional capabilities through supported software updates.

Continued innovation in automotive operating systems, cloud connectivity, cybersecurity, and advanced driving applications is expected to support long-term industry development. Software-defined vehicles are positioned to become a central part of next-generation automotive design, creating opportunities for established manufacturers, technology companies, and emerging software providers.

data.description:
(Updates with afternoon trading levels)
    * LatAm currencies hit 10 month low
    * Brazil Senate backs fiscal package, easing debt concerns
    * Mexico data signals resilience despite peso's recent weakness

    By Tharuniyaa Lakshmi and Avinash  P
       Nov 19 (Reuters) - MSCI's index of Latin American equities slipped to a one-year low on Thursday amid fragile global sentiment, while growing expectations of tighter US interest rates weighed on regional currencies.‌
    The index fell 2.72% to its weakest since late November 2025.
    "These don't seem like fundamental bottom-up moves. It seems like short-term macro sentiment, which is creating high levels of correlation across different asset classes," said Malcolm Dorson, head of EM strategy at Global X.
     "Fed governors, including Governor Waller, have said inflation remains heading in the wrong direction. So it's not just emerging markets. Risk assets in general have been on edge."
    Brazil's benchmark Bovespa index fell 1% as losses in the energy sector weighedon the benchmark.
    Investors also assessed the Brazil Senate's approval of a fiscal package aimed at meeting the government's fiscal targets, although many viewed the measures as only an initial step toward improving the country's debt outlook.
    Brazilian President Lula da Silva criticized market participants for profiting from speculation over his cabinet picks. Brazilian assets have sold off since his reelection.
     Brazil's real slipped 0.9% to a fresh April 2025 low.
     The broader index of Latin American currencies fell 1.96% to a 10- month low.
    Investors have largely priced in a quarter-point rate hike from the Federal Reserve in December, helping lift the dollar to multi-month highs and putting pressure on emerging-market currencies across the board.
    A stronger dollar weighs on developing-market currencies by drawing capital into US assets and away from riskier markets.‌
    In Mexico, the peso fell 1.5% against the US dollar as investors weighed the widening monetary policy divergence between the Federal Reserve and the Bank of Mexico after the Fed raised interest rates in September for the first time in three years, while Banxico delivered a quarter-percentage-point rate cut earlier this month.
    Despite the currency's weakness, data from national statistics agency INEGI pointed to resilience in Mexico's economy, with a preliminary estimate showing economic activity likely expanded 2.3% in October from a year earlier.
    Chile's peso fell 0.7%, though analysts pointed to upside potential for the currency.
    "We have a bullish view on the Chilean peso. This is our preferred strategy in a scenario of falling global oil prices. Risks are weaker copper prices, US tariffs on refined copper, and lower-than-expected economic growth," said Ezequiel Aguirre, head of LatAm FX and rates strategy at BofA Global Research.
    In the US, Anthropic briefly topped a $2 trillion market valuation in its market debut, but initial enthusiasm waned as concerns over the durability of the AI trade, which has driven sentiment recently, weighed on risk appetite.
    Elsewhere, Ukraine's bonds also weakened, highlighting lingering investor concerns over geopolitical risks despite signs of progress on the diplomatic front.​‌​‌
    Separately, South Africa's central bank held its key interest rate in a split decision, with its governor saying monetary policy was tight enough after two hikes this year.

data.title: Bending Spoons has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Mailchimp
data.description:
MILAN--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Bending Spoons S.p.A. has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Mailchimp, the email marketing automation platform for businesses, from Intuit, the global financial technology platform, at an enterprise value of $3.68 billion. In connection with the all-cash transaction, Intuit will invest $368 million of its proceeds into newly issued Bending Spoons equity. The acquisition, including the investment, is subject to customary closing conditions, including regulatory approvals.

“Mailchimp is a powerful brand, built over two decades of reshaping the email marketing category and redefining how companies grow their audiences,” said Luca Ferrari, Bending Spoons CEO and co-founder. “We’re honored to welcome it to Bending Spoons and excited about what we can accomplish together. After closing, we’ll invest substantially in the business, building on the powerful, easy-to-use tools customers already value and rely on.”

“Mailchimp has helped millions of businesses grow and acquire customers through email marketing automation, and we are grateful to the Mailchimp team for what they have built and the impact they have had on customers and Intuit,” said Jack Tam, Senior Vice President, Intuit. “We are confident Bending Spoons will lead Mailchimp to continued success in this next chapter. We are focused on ensuring a smooth transition for Mailchimp’s customers, partners, and employees.”

Details of the Proposed Transaction

Under the terms of the agreement, which was unanimously approved by the board of directors of Bending Spoons, Bending Spoons will acquire the Mailchimp business by purchasing 100% of The Rocket Science Group, LLC and other assets and liabilities of the Mailchimp business.

The transaction is expected to close in early 2027, subject to receipt of required regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions.

Legal Counsel and Financial Advisors

Citi and J.P. Morgan are acting as co-lead financial advisors to Bending Spoons, and Goldman Sachs Bank Europe SE, Succursale Italia and UniCredit are acting as financial advisors on the transaction. Freshfields US LLP is serving as legal counsel to Bending Spoons, EY-Parthenon is providing financial due diligence services and EY STP tax due diligence services, and NewTeam is providing financial services.

About Bending Spoons

Bending Spoons is built on the conviction that operational excellence enables efficient growth through acquisitions. It acquires digital businesses, implements deep transformations and ongoing optimizations to sustainably expand earnings, and reinvests in additional acquisitions, thereby continuing the compounding cycle. The company has executed this strategy for more than a decade and, to date, has never sold a material business.

Bending Spoons strives to envision the most successful version of an acquired business, and works to close the gap between its current state and that vision as quickly and completely as possible. The transformation is typically deep and entails reorganizing teams, overhauling technology, redesigning user interfaces, accelerating product development, and enhancing marketing and monetization. AI is often both a central component of the vision and a key tool in implementing the transformation.

Bending Spoons’ performance is driven by its Platform—comprising its people, proprietary technologies, and proprietary data—and reflects an intense focus on achieving exceptional talent density, cultural strength, and technical capabilities.

Bending Spoons’ main businesses include Airtable, AOL, Brightcove, Eventbrite, Evernote, Miro, Tractive, Vimeo, and WeTransfer.

data.title: Fed's Goolsbee says AI surge could strain US capacity, overheat economy
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 19 (Reuters) - The booming rollout of artificial intelligence technology could strain the US economy's capacity and further boost inflation that the Federal Reserve will have to counteract, Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said on Thursday, as AI firm Anthropic set a new record for an initial public offering of stock.

"The AI boom is contributing to the potential of overheating in the economy. I find it hard to ... look at that any other way," Goolsbee said in a conference call with reporters. "When you're getting major business investment, almost unprecedented levels of business investment, there's a high danger that the economy's capacity cannot handle that kind of a pig through the python."

(Reporting by Howard Schneider; Editing by Paul Simao)

data.title: US court ruling jeopardizes Sentinel Midstream's license for deepwater oil export project
data.description:
* Court says Texas GulfLink application area overlapped Enterprise's SPOT project area

* Sentinel is working with MARAD to discuss its options for moving forward, source says

* Sentinel cannot continue with the current license, source says

* Company expects construction schedule to proceed as planned

By Arathy Somasekhar

HOUSTON, Nov 19 (Reuters) - A court ruling has jeopardized a license for Sentinel Midstream's $2.1 billion deepwater crude oil export project off the Texas coast, an environmental group that petitioned the court said this week.

The ruling, which took effect on October 30, poses a setback and likely delays for the oil transportation and storage company, which has already started work on the project. It could also impact other pending deepwater port applications.

In August, a US appeals court voided a federal record of decision for Sentinel Midstream's Texas GulfLink project, citing overlap with another deepwater project.

An official at Sentinel Midstream said work would continue on the project, characterizing it as "business as usual." But a source with knowledge of the situation said the company could not continue with the offshore project on the current license.

Last year, the US Maritime Administration (MARAD), in its record of decision (ROD), approved Texas GulfLink with conditions and the company received its license in January 2026. President Donald Trump has pushed for faster project approvals to bolster the US energy industry. Sentinel made a final investment decision in May and began construction.

MARAD's record of decision approving Texas GulfLink's application violated the Deepwater Port Act's requirement that only one deepwater port be approved per application area, the 5th US Circuit Court of Appeals said. Texas GulfLink's application area, when properly designated, would have intersected with Enterprise Products Partners' Sea Port Oil Terminal (SPOT) deepwater project.

Congress has struck a careful balance between promoting and regulating the construction and operation of deepwater ports, the court said, holding that the Deepwater Port Act requires an application area to encompass the entirety of a proposed deepwater port site, including any proposed pipeline.

"The Court's decision is clear: it vacated the record of decision that was the foundation of GulfLink's license. Now, MARAD has to revoke or suspend that license," Michael Brown, a counsel for the petitioners, said on Wednesday.

Construction of the project cannot continue without a federal deepwater port license, said environmental group Better Brazoria Clean Air and Water in a press release this week.

MARAD said it was disappointed with the outcome and continues to pursue all avenues to achieve the President's vision of American energy dominance.

"Sentinel is working with MARAD to discuss its options for moving forward. The company cannot continue with the current license," a source familiar with the matter said.

In comments to Reuters this week, Sentinel said its license has not been suspended or terminated.

Texas GulfLink, to be situated about 30 miles off Freeport, Texas, remains on track for a fourth-quarter 2028 operational date, Bruce Heine, a senior vice president at Sentinel, said this week, adding that given the narrow nature and scope of the issue, there are multiple paths to address the statutory concern without disrupting ongoing construction activities or overall project schedule.

"It remains business as usual for Texas GulfLink, with site development and improvement activities currently underway at our Jones Creek onshore terminal facility as we prepare to commence tank construction," Heine said, adding that major long-lead equipment and pipe have been purchased, and key construction contracts executed.

However, the company in its motion last month to stay the court mandate said that the Texas GulfLink's license expressly incorporates the ROD as a compliance standard, adding that voiding the ROD in turn exposed the license to suspension or revocation by MARAD, and prevents construction of offshore components.

"At a minimum, the cloud on Texas GulfLink's regulatory posture will harm Texas GulfLink in the marketplace," the company said then, adding that "given the uncertainty of its ROD and license, Texas GulfLink will not commence construction of the deepwater port under the current posture, even if the mandate is stayed."

Texas GulfLink plans to petition the Supreme Court, the company said in its motion. It added that there are two other pending deepwater ports under review with application areas similar to Texas GulfLink's that will likely require redesignation as a result of the panel's decision, potentially resulting in consequential impacts to those projects as well.

If Sentinel is required to resubmit its application, it would have to await a new ROD and license. While it took nearly seven years for Sentinel to secure approvals last time, MARAD has sped up its approval process under US President Donald Trump. It recently issued a deepwater project application license in just 410 days, nearly 3.7 years faster than ​the historical average.

The Texas GulfLink project aims to fully load a supertanker with about 2 million barrels of oil per day. The administration in recent weeks also approved deepwater port license applications for Energy Transfer's Blue Marlin Offshore Port, an oil export project off the Louisiana coast, and for ST LNG, which aims to ship liquefied natural gas off ​the Texas coast.

(Reporting by Arathy Somasekhar in Houston; additional reporting by David Shepardson; Editing by Liz Hampton and David Gregorio)

data.title: US signed off on sales of nearly 900,000 AI chips to China in six months-committee
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 19 (Reuters) - The Trump administration approved shipments of nearly 900,000 advanced AI chips made by Nvidia and AMD for Chinese companies from December 2025 through May 2026, the House Foreign Affairs Committee said on Thursday.

The approvals for 879,000 chip shipmentsby the Commerce Department included 75,000 for Alibaba ( BABA ), 150,000 for Tencent ( TCTZF ), 43,000 for Baidu ( BIDU ), and 4,000 for BYD, the committee said. Companies had sought permission to ship 3.4 million of them to China total during the period, committee documents show.

The unusual release of chip export licensing data comes as the administration of President Donald Trump faces heightened scrutiny following revelations about former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy, which fueled renewed calls for a tougher stance against Chinese technology threats.

All four of the Chinese companies highlighted in the committee report are on the Pentagon list of alleged Chinese military-backed companies.

The committee chair, Brian Mast, has "exercised his authorities under the Export Control Reform Act to publicly reveal export control license application information regarding NVIDIA and AMD's AI chip licenses for the People's Republic of China," the committee said in a statement. It was not immediately clear how many of the approvals resulted in actual China-bound shipment of the chips, which included Nvidia's ( NVDA ) H200 and AMD's equivalent MI325X.

Nvidia said in a statement that the approvals were "subject to strict conditions and limited volumes." It added that "despite receiving some licenses, we have since stopped shipping H200s to China."

AMD did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

(Reporting by Alexandra Alper, Ryan Patrick Jones, Katharine Jackson; editing by Scott Malone and Chris Sanders)

data.title: California faces mounting deficit and AI bubble risks, analyst warns
data.description:
Despite a recent AI-fueled revenue surge, California remains ill-prepared for a potential economic downturn or stock market correction the Legislative Analyst’s Office said in its independent assessment of the state’s fiscal outlook Wednesday.

The LAO delivers a fiscal outlook to state lawmakers annually ahead of the governor’s budget introduction in January.

Although high-tech gains have buoyed general fund collections in the short term, Legislative Analyst Gabriel Petek said the state has an underlying structural imbalance. 

California faces a $2 billion deficit at the end of 2027-28 — which Petek described as “modest” compared to last year’s projected $18 billion deficit — but long-term shortfalls could expand significantly if market volatility persists, according to the LAO’s November fiscal report.

“The state is facing a budget deficit for the fifth year in a row despite being at record revenue levels,” Petek said during the briefing. “The budget problem for the first year is fairly small, but grows to $30 billion by 2028-29.”

The primary concern is California’s reliance on personal income tax revenues derived from capital gains and stock market performance, Petek said. With stock indexes up substantially since 2022, indicators — such as margin debt and price-to-earnings ratios — match levels not seen since the dot-com bubble of the late 1990s, he said.

“The theme of this report is the stock market is a looming risk to this budget,” Petek said. 

“The stock market has been booming since 2022,” he said. “We have seen the stock market go up by 150%. State income tax revenues have grown at twice the normal rate. It’s been a good run.”

The problem is that everything the LAO’s office is tracking in terms of economic indicators show the stock market has moved into “classic speculative bubble territory,” Petek said.

While baseline estimates show near-term revenues up by $11 billion over June projections, constitutional spending mandates — such as Proposition 98 school funding and Proposition 2 reserve requirements — offset those gains, Petek said. Fast-growing state commitments in Health and Human Services, including In-Home Supportive Services (IHSS), Medi-Cal, and childcare, continue to put ongoing pressure on the budget, he said.

To illustrate the severity of a potential crash scenario reminiscent of the 2001 or 2008 downturns, legislative analysts modeled a severe market drop by 2027, Petek said. Under that scenario, state revenues could fall $130 billion below baseline projections, creating annual budget deficits near $35 billion, he said.

Addressing a shortfall of that magnitude under a severe recession would require drastic measures, he said.

Generating $50 billion in solutions would be akin to the Legislature undoing virtually all discretionary service expansions enacted since 2019, or enacting tax increases larger than recent ballot measures, Petek said.

To safeguard California’s fiscal position ahead of the governor's budget proposal in January, the Legislative Analyst’s Office urged lawmakers to adopt prudent revenue assumptions, maximize reserves, and focus on structural fixes rather than reliance on temporary maneuvers.

“Our central message is the state budget is overextended at this point,” Petek stated. “We think the Legislature should seek to right-size the budget rather than covering it through one-time maneuvers.”

data.title: EXPLAINER-Could Huang, Nvidia and company's board be held liable over affair scandal?
data.description:
(Adds details on Alice Huang, possible state and SEC actions)

By Tom Hals

WILMINGTON, Delaware, Nov 19 (Reuters) - Reports that Jensen Huang, the co-founder of AI chip powerhouse Nvidia ( NVDA ), had an extramarital affair with a company executive and ties to a suspected Chinese spy have led to his resignation as CEO and sparked investigations by the US securities regulator and FBI, calls for congressional hearings, a review by the company's independent directors and a proposed investor class action lawsuit.

Below is a look at the potential legal exposure for Huang, Nvidia ( NVDA ) and the directors of the company, which dominates the global market for computer chips that power the AI economy.

WHAT ARE THE ALLEGATIONS?

Huang had a relationship with Alice Huang, an unrelated former executive of ​Singapore-based company Megaspeed, and US intelligence agencies are trying to determine her ties to China's Ministry of State Security, according to two people familiar with the matter. Megaspeed has faced US scrutiny over suspicions that it helped Beijing gain access to Nvidia's ( NVDA ) advanced AI chips that are subject to US export restrictions.

Huang admitted he was unfaithful to his wife without providing details about the relationship, which led to a drop in Nvidia's ( NVDA ) stock price. US President Donald Trump said Huang told him that he had no idea that the woman was a spy and Huang has not been accused of criminal wrongdoing.

Reuters could not independently verify the intelligence allegation, which China's foreign ministry has said was "groundless."

Nvidia ( NVDA ) formed an independent committee of directors that hired the Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to assist in an internal investigation.

Huang resigned on November 11 after reports that he had an extramarital affair with a company executive who reported to him.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) sits at the center of the ​technological rivalry between the United States and China. Washington has imposed restrictions on exports of advanced AI chips to China since ​2022. News of the affair has emerged as Democrats seized control of Congress in the November 3 midterm elections, propelled in part by anti-AI and anti-corruption sentiment.

WHAT ABOUT FEDERAL SECURITIES FRAUD?

A proposed class action was filed in San Jose, California, federal court on November 9 alleging the company and Huang defrauded shareholders by concealing Huang's alleged relationship with Alice Huang and Megaspeed, which Jensen Huang described in an October 30 Bloomberg interview as "normal and not unusual."

Securities fraud plaintiffs must show that Nvidia ( NVDA ) and Huang knowingly misled investors, that investors relied on those misleading statements and that those misleading statements artificially inflated the stock.

The lawsuit did not specify damages but the stock lost around 20% from its peak to the end of the class period, a decline of around $1 trillion in market value.

Such lawsuits are often filed in the wake of a company's stock suffering a large drop, and more are likely.

While the vast majority of US public companies have insurance against securities lawsuits, Nvidia ( NVDA ) does not given its huge financial resources.

WHAT ABOUT STATE LAW VIOLATIONS?

Missouri Attorney General Catherine Hanaway, a Republican, is investigating whether Huang's actions harmed state pension funds and her office said they were looking at it through a consumer protection lens focused on potential misrepresentations.

California Attorney General Rob Bonta told Bloomberg that the Nvidia ( NVDA ) crisis raised red flags and his office could investigate. Bonta's office did not respond to a request for further details.

State officials could use state securities laws to pursue investigations of alleged violations, according to legal experts. New York's Martin Act is considered the most powerful and the state's attorneys general have used it to police Wall Street, including an insider trading case brought this year. The Martin Act also allows the attorney general to pursue criminal claims.

No states have brought claims and the New York attorney general did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

COULD THE SEC STEP IN?

The US Securities and Exchange Commission launched a civil investigation that included whether Nvidia ( NVDA ) misled investors, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing people familiar with the situation. Reuters has not verified the report.

The regulator would have a lower burden of proof than a private investor class action and the SEC can obtain alternative remedies, such as barring individuals from serving as officers or directors of public companies.

In 2022, during the administration of Democratic President Joe Biden, Nvidia ( NVDA ) settled allegations by the SEC that in 2018 it had made inadequate disclosures regarding the growth of its processors for the gaming market. The company paid a $5.5 million fine but did not admit or deny the allegations. An investor class action lawsuit over the same allegations is ongoing.

The SEC declined to comment.

COULD THE BOARD BE HELD LIABLE?

An investor filed a so-called derivative lawsuit on November 11 seeking to hold the board liable for failing to make a good faith effort to oversee the business and Huang. The lawsuit said the board allowed Nvidia ( NVDA ) to make repeated assurances about the company's dealings with Megaspeed and the board did not act on warning signs about Huang's relationship with Alice Huang until it was public.

The lawsuit, filed in federal court in the Northern District of California, also said the board lacked independence to investigate Huang.

Huang's resignation could strengthen the board's defenses against derivative lawsuits by showing the directors were acting on signs of misconduct by forcing him out and refusing to consider his return.

Investors, including state pension funds, can also use their shareholder rights to seek internal records to investigate the board and look for potential conflicts.

The board could sue Huang for any fines or securities fraud settlements that result from the scandal. For example, electric truck maker Nikola took legal action and got a judgment of $168 million against its former CEO Trevor Milton.

CAN SECURITIES FRAUD CARRY CRIMINAL PENALTIES?

Only a small fraction of all securities fraud cases lead to criminal charges, as most violations are handled through civil or administrative enforcement.

But a federal statute, enacted as part of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002, criminalizes schemes that knowingly defraud investors through false pretenses. Prosecutors would need to show that Huang intentionally lied to the public about the affair in order to keep Nvidia's ( NVDA ) stock price from falling, rather than for personal reasons such as avoiding embarrassment.

US Attorney General Todd Blanche also said the FBI was investigating if Alice Huang was a spy.

If Huang knew about Alice Huang's alleged intelligence connection, he could face criminal liability under the Economic Espionage Act, a 1996 law that punishes the misappropriation of trade secrets to benefit a foreign government.

(Reporting by Tom Hals in Wilmington, Delaware; Additional reporting by Jan Wolfe and Steve Holland; Editing by Nick Zieminski and Noleen Walder)

data.title: New York sues IHG, others over Holiday Inn accused of exploiting immigrant workers
data.description:
* Suit says workers forced to work up to 112 hours a week, often without pay

* New York attorney general seeks damages, civil fines

* IHG condemns trafficking, denies knowledge of serious misconduct

By Jonathan Stempel

NEW YORK, Nov 19 (Reuters) - New York's attorney general on Thursday sued InterContinental Hotels Group ( IHG ), as well as the owner of a former Holiday Inn in downtown Rochester, New York, accusing them of exploiting dozens of immigrant workers.

Attorney General Letitia James said workers recruited to renovate the hotel were required to work as many as 112 hours a week after renovations began in the spring of 2023, with some going at least eight months without being paid.

James also said the workers and their families, including children, were forced to live in pest- and vermin-infested rooms on the abandoned seventh floor that had no heat, electricity, working toilets or running water. She said the owner and a renovation contractor threatened workers who demanded wages with eviction and deportation.

IHG was accused of benefiting from the renovations and knowing about the threats and forced labor, including through managers who spoke with some of the workers during an inspection.

James said this contradicted IHG's website, which says the British company is committed to combating forced labor, human trafficking and other forms of the "terrible, often hidden crime" of modern slavery.

"A company that calls itself a leader in the fight against human trafficking cannot look away when workers inside its own hotel ask for help," James said in a statement.

IHG DENIES KNOWLEDGE OF MISCONDUCT

In a statement, IHG said it strongly condemns trafficking in any form, and the allegations in the lawsuit "represent a profound violation of IHG's values, culture, and expectations" with anyone associated with the company.

"We agree that the hotel owner and contractor should be held responsible for any violations of the law," IHG said. "We emphatically deny that IHG had any knowledge of serious misconduct by the hotel owner or contractor as alleged in the lawsuit."

The lawsuit seeks a variety of damages and civil fines for alleged violations of New York labor and executive laws and a federal law protecting trafficking victims.

Other defendants include Nayan Patel, who bought the hotel in December 2020 and operated it under a license from IHG, and the contractor Roman Petrik. It is unclear whether they have lawyers.

Patel did not immediately return a phone message left at an address obtained through a public records search. Petrik could not immediately be reached for comment.

The hotel was rebranded a Wyndham in January 2025, and Rochester officials closed it in June 2026 because of fire code and other violations.

IHG has more than 7,000 hotels in more than 100 countries, and dozens of brands including Candlewood Suites, Crowne Plaza, Hotel Indigo and Kimpton.

(Reporting by Jonathan Stempel in New York; Additional reporting by Doyinsola Oladipo, Editing by Alexia Garamfalvi and Jonathan Spicer )

data.title: Taiwan's Stock Pickers Are Walking Out to Bet Their Own Money
data.description:
NEW YORK, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fly On Wall Street News Commentary - Taiwan's benchmark stock index was up 62% this year, the best showing of any major equity gauge in the world, when Bloomberg reported on Oct. 16 that some of the island's professional fund managers and analysts are quitting their jobs to invest their own money. Strict rules keep them from trading the very stocks they pick for clients, and in a year when about one in ten stocks in the index has more than doubled, some have decided the trade-off is no longer worth it. Companies and funds mentioned in this article include: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited ( TSM ) [TSMC] , ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. ( ASX ) [ASE] , United Microelectronics Corporation ( UMC ) [UMC] , iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF , The Taiwan Fund, Inc. ( TWN ) .

Watching From Behind the Locker

Taiwan does not ban personal investing outright, but its asset-management code of conduct bars staff from trading a locally listed stock or a linked derivative within seven business days before or after their firm's funds trade it, which in practice rules out personal stock-picking. Fund managers must also lock away their phones, laptops and smartwatches each morning until the market closes at 1:30 p.m. The phone rule was formalized in 2024 to deter insider trading, the Taipei Times reported in July, after six former fund managers from four firms were indicted for front-running trades through the accounts of relatives and friends.

Ken Tsai, 40, a fund manager who until July worked at a large Taiwanese asset manager that Bloomberg did not name, told Bloomberg he made a Taiwanese maker of AI-server data-transfer components his fund's largest holding in 2024. The stock rose more than fivefold in 2025 and about sixfold again this year, but he owned none of it personally. "It left me with a strong sense of relative deprivation," he said. He now works at a private investment firm in Taipei, which was also not named. Pay adds to the pull: Taiwan portfolio managers earn roughly US$124,000 to US$311,000 a year, well below Hong Kong base salaries, according to Bloomberg, citing headhunters and recruitment-firm data.

The private shops they are joining sit outside those rules. They register as private companies with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and do not need asset-management licenses from the Financial Supervisory Commission because they do not raise public money. Brokers told Bloomberg some of them now generate more than NT$10 billion in monthly trading volume, rivaling mid-sized asset managers.

The Rally Behind the Exits

Much of the rally traces back to the AI hardware supply chain. TSMC reported third-quarter revenue of NT$1.49 trillion (US$46.7 billion) on Oct. 15, up 50.9% from a year earlier, while net income jumped 68.7% and gross margin reached 66.4%. It guided fourth-quarter revenue from US$52.3 billion to US$54.3 billion.

Chip packaging and testing has ridden the same wave. ASE Technology ( ASX ) reported September net revenue of NT$88.1 billion, up 45.5% from a year earlier, and third-quarter revenue of NT$244.2 billion, up 44.8%.

Mature-node foundry UMC reported August sales up 30.71% from a year earlier, lifting year-to-date sales 14.66%. In its second-quarter report, the company guided for capacity utilization above 90% in the third quarter and said revenue from its 22/28nm business continues to set record highs.

CONTINUED... Read more market coverage at: flyonwallstreet.com

A Talent Squeeze, Not a Stampede

The numbers point to churn more than an exodus. Fewer than half of Taiwan's 20 largest local equity mutual funds have kept the same portfolio manager for more than three years, according to fund-data site MoneyDJ, and Bloomberg reported that applications for junior roles at some international firms have roughly halved this year. Yet the FSC said the industry's registered headcount actually rose to 4,729 in September from 4,581 at the end of 2025. Firms are responding: the largest foreign asset manager in Taiwan is offering cross-market analyst roles and office rotations to keep staff.

Regulators are paying attention. The FSC said on Oct. 15 it is gathering information and plans to review the rules, balancing market development against conflicts of interest and investor protection. One asset-management executive told Bloomberg there is no easy solution for now.

The Case for the Pros

At least one professionally managed fund has kept pace. The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ), a closed-end fund listed in New York, reported a 47.36% total return for its fiscal quarter ended May 31, against 26.12% for the TAIEX Total Return Index over the same period, with net asset value of US$116.90 a share at the end of that quarter.

Investors who prefer to own the whole market can use the iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF, which holds about US$11.9 billion in assets.

Last week was a reminder of how quickly the math can change. The TAIEX fell 4.6%, its first weekly decline in five weeks, as a technology selloff spread and TSMC CEO C.C. Wei warned of macroeconomic uncertainty and weak consumer demand, according to Trading Economics. In New York, TSMC's shares fell 8.98% from the Oct. 9 close to $412.61 on Oct. 16, ASE dropped 14.86% to $39.53, UMC slid 13.68% to $19.82, the iShares fund lost 7.04% to $106.26 and The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ) declined 8.78% to $94.18, according to Stock Analysis data. For the managers who just traded a salary for their own account, those swings now land on them.

Nov 19 (Field Level Media) - Mark Walter, who has a controlling stake in the Los Angeles Dodgers, is set to sell off another sports asset, with Sportico reporting Thursday he is close to a deal to offload the WNBA's Los Angeles Sparks for $750 million.

San Diego Padres owners Jose E. Feliciano and wife Kwanza Jones reportedly are set to purchase the Sparks in a record deal for a WNBA team. The previous largest purchase price for an WNBA team came when the Connecticut Sun were sold for $300 million in March of this year. The Sun plan to move to Houston.

The Sparks were purchased for $10 million in 2014 by a group led by Walter. Former NBA star Magic Johnson also was listed among the ownership group.

Since Walter's insurance firms have been under investigation, Walter has sold his majority stake in the Los Angeles Lakers in a reported $12.5 billion deal in August, and his 13% stake in Chelsea of the English Premier League. Reports indicate he could be looking for a buyer for his stake in the Cadillac Formula 1 team that was recently valued at $3 billion.

Walter has a 27% controlling stake in the Dodgers, with the Los Angeles Times reporting earlier this month that he has no plans to sell his investment in the MLB club. Earlier this year, Sportico valued the Dodgers at over $9 billion.

Feliciano and Jones officially purchased the Padres in August for $3.9 billion.

(--Field Level Media)

data.title: Exclusive-Trump administration weighs forcing US firms to disclose Chinese AI use
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 18 (Reuters) - The Trump administration is considering requiring US companies to publicly disclose their use of Chinese AI models, a bid to discourage reliance on the technology without imposing new restrictions that could anger industry or Beijing, three people told Reuters.

The Treasury Department and the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP) have discussed the plan, which would apply to companies such as Airbnb ( ABNB ), the people said. The company uses Qwen, an AI model made by China's Alibaba ( BABA ), to power its AI customer service agent.

Under the plan, companies like Airbnb ( ABNB ) would be required to post that information on their websites. 

It was not immediately clear if the idea was gaining traction within the administration or if it would be enshrined in a formal rulemaking process if it does move forward.

But its consideration, first reported by Reuters, underscores an emerging push within the administration toward combating the spread of powerful Chinese open weight models, a source of deep concern within the government. Open weight models make their core components publicly available for anyone to download and adapt.

The proposal also shows officials are looking at ways to discourage use of Chinese AI through a "name and shame" campaign while sticking to a broader anti-regulation stance on AI.

The White House, the Treasury Department and Alibaba ( BABA ) did not respond to requests for comment. Airbnb ( ABNB ) said in a statement that its AI activity "runs overwhelmingly on U.S.-origin models" and the company uses "only a limited number of China-origin models, all of which are open-source and run only through approved U.S.-based service providers, keeping data and operations separate and protected." 

The Chinese Embassy in Washington said Beijing opposes politicizing trade and tech issues, which will "only stifle global AI advances and serve no one's interests. We will resolutely safeguard Chinese businesses' lawful rights and interests," it added.

The consideration comes as revelations about Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy have fueled renewed calls in Washington for a tougher stance on China. They have turned a spotlight on cases of ​Nvidia AI chips being smuggled to China that went unpunished, dialing up pressure on the Trump administration to crack down on Chinese tech threats.

Chinese-made open-weight models are gaining ground with US companies because they are cheaper than proprietary AI tools from top US labs OpenAI and Anthropic, and perform well enough.

But China hawks fear Beijing is using such models - like Moonshot AI's Kimi, DeepSeek or Qwen - to hook US companies so they will become dependent on Chinese AI.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in July that the Trump administration could sanction Chinese AI companies if they were found to be guilty of intellectual property theft via distillation of American models. Distillation is the process of training smaller ​AI models ⁠using the output of larger ones as part of an effort to lower the costs of training a powerful new AI tool.

Bessent's remarks echoed comments in April by Michael Kratsios, OSTP director, who accused China of stealing US artificial ​intelligence labs' intellectual property on an "industrial scale," spurring a State Department-led push to highlight such behavior to foreign counterparts. 

CONGRESSIONAL INVESTIGATION

But US officials have stopped short of restricting or taking punitive action against Chinese AI companies.

The issue has attracted the attention of Congress. Republican US Representatives Andrew Garbarino of New York and John Moolenaar of Michigan, who chair the House Homeland Security Committee and the House select committee on China, respectively, launched an investigation into American companies' use of Chinese AI this year. 

They sent letters to Airbnb ( ABNB ) as well as Anysphere, the maker of the AI coding tool Cursor, whose Composer 2 AI model was built on a version of Kimi. A letter was also sent to DoorDash ( DASH ), whose co-founder said the company routes some tasks in an internal system through Kimi.

Moonshot, DoorDash ( DASH ), and SpaceX, which bought Anysphere, did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Moolenaar welcomed news of the Trump administration's deliberations. "Disclosure is an important step in managing the potential risks posed by the diffusion of Chinese open-weight models in the United States," he said in a statement to Reuters, noting that risks remain even if US companies run Chinese AI models on their own infrastructure.

Canada-based Thomson Reuters ( TMSOF ) , which owns Reuters, also uses Alibaba's ( BABA ) Qwen, according to a TR spokesperson. She noted that the model was "substantially retrained" to align "with our standards for safety, accuracy and neutrality," and runs entirely within the company's own infrastructure.

Chinese AI models were the three most popular by token usage in October on OpenRouter, an AI marketplace platform that tracks usage data. Tokens are units of data processed by AI models. 

Chinese AI models have even been used by the US government itself. Reuters reported in September that a US government website deployed an AI model from China's Alibaba ( BABA ) to allow users to search proposed federal regulations even though the FBI accused the model's developer of copying Anthropic's technology. 

American open-weight models include Meta's Muse Glimmer, Nvidia's ( NVDA ) Nemotron and Reflection AI's Beam. 

(Reporting by Alexandra Alper; Additional Reporting by Courtney Rozen; editing by Chris Sanders and Sanjeev Miglani)

data.description:
TORONTO, Nov 19 (Reuters) - The Canadian dollar steadied near an earlier 19-month low against its US counterpart on Thursday as risk aversion rose and ahead of domestic retail sales data that could help guide expectations for Bank of Canada interest rate hikes.

The loonie was trading nearly unchanged at 1.4332 per US dollar, or 69.77 US cents, after touching its weakest intraday level since April 2025 at 1.43575.

* US stock indexes tumbled after Anthropic's blockbuster market debut failed to ease concerns about the AI trade, triggering a broader market selloff.

* "You've got a little bit of risk aversion in the market - that's bullish for the US dollar," said Rahim Madhavji, president at Knightsbridge Foreign Exchange. "The loonie is struggling to find catalysts that are going to help it."

* The price of oil, one of Canada's major exports, rose 0.7% to $83.84 a barrel as investors focused on fresh reports of tanker disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. Still, oil has pulled back sharply from its October peak.

* "The dominant themes are interest rate diversion, oil prices are a bit of a headwind, US dollar strength," Madhavji said.

* Investors have fully discounted an interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve next month and are leaning toward further tightening in January, swap market data shows. Chances the Bank of Canada would hike in December are seen at 67%.

* Canadian retail sales data for September, due on Friday, could help guide BoC rate hike expectations. Economists expect a month-over-month increase of 0.7%.

* Canadian bond yields were mixed across a steeper curve, with the 10-year up 1.2 basis point at 3.814%.

* In the corporate bond market, Alphabet was set to raise billions of Canadian dollars in a debt sale. Pricing of the multi-tranche deal was expected later on Thursday, a Canadian bond market source said.

(Reporting by Fergal Smith, Editing by Nick Zieminski)

data.title: Anthropic tops SpaceX with record $2 trillion Nasdaq debut
data.description:
Nov 19 (Reuters) - Anthropic notched a valuation of about $2 trillion in its Nasdaq debut on Thursday, vaulting past SpaceX's massive June listing and capping a turbulent stretch for the AI sector that tested Wall Street's appetite for the technology.

The early exuberance, however, partly faded, signaling volatility ahead as investors locked in quick gains and the main indexes retreated amid renewed jitters over the sector's outlook.

Shares of the world's first publicly traded frontier AI company opened at $111.5, 34% higher than the IPO price of $83. But the stock pared its gains and was last trading around $99.

The AI euphoria has somewhat cooled in recent weeks, marked by Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang's exit, but now shifts Wall Street's spotlight on to its rival OpenAI as the industry's next major public listing.

"We like the enterprise AI narrative, but we do not like overpaying for market sentiment. It isn't a prudent 'buy-at-any-price' opportunity for retail wealth clients," said Talley Leger, chief market strategist at The Wealth Consulting Group.

"History shows that retail investors buying hot tech IPOs on day one historically underperform broad market indexes over a 3-year horizon."

AI technology has boosted economic growth, but sparked doomsday warnings and arguably helped usher in a data-center-skeptic Democratic tsunami in the US midterm elections.

Investors who once embraced the boom have turned skeptical in recent weeks over concerns that the enormous spending needed to build out the sector and the mounting debt loads may not be justified by the eventual returns.

Anthropic, too, has signaled it may tap debt markets.

"At some point in the future we're hoping to be investment grade, and debt is an instrument that we have available to us, and we'd like to use at some point in the future," CEO Dario Amodei told CNBC in an interview.

AN INDUSTRY BENCHMARK

As the first frontier AI company to go public, Anthropic is poised to become the sector's benchmark. The company sold 980 million shares at $83 each, pricing the IPO above its initial range of $70 to $78 set when it launched the road show.

Its IPO proceeds could climb to as much as $93.5 billion if underwriters fully exercise their option to purchase additional shares.

Currently, the figure sits at over $107 billion, including the additional $26 billion raised through a private placement. AMD, Broadcom, Alphabet's Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia ( NVDA ) and TSMC were the investors in the private placement.

"Some of the demand may simply reflect investors not wanting to miss out on the rare opportunity to gain exposure to a leading AI company, even if its long-term profitability remains uncertain," IPOX associate Lukas Muehlbauer said.

London-based index rebalance analytics firm Intropic estimates passive demand from index-tracking funds will account for the purchase of up to 30% of Anthropic's shares offered by the end of the year.

Anthropic also joins the trillion-dollar club, stacked with behemoths such as Microsoft, Apple and Nvidia ( NVDA ).

The blockbuster deal is going to earn the underwriters, led by Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, a $550 million fee, a regulatory filing showed.

BIG PAYDAY FOR CO-FOUNDERS

Anthropic's IPO is set to create thousands of paper millionaires and a handful of billionaires.

Based on the IPO price, CEO Amodei and his six co-founders, who together own about 10% of the company, had stakes worth nearly $150 billion combined, according to a Reuters calculation based on details in the filing.

More broadly, the listing is expected to create a wave of new wealth across the AI sector, rewarding everyone from early researchers and engineers to administrative staff.

JUSTIFYING THE PRICE TAG

Debate has intensified across global markets in recent months over whether the AI boom is veering into bubble territory, with economists, CEOs and political leaders split over its sustainability.

Much of the scrutiny has focused on circular financing arrangements. A complicated web of deals between AI companies, chipmakers, cloud providers and investors has raised questions over how much of the industry's growth is being fueled by money circulating within the same ecosystem.

Anthropic's breakneck growth has so far defied these concerns, but some investors have said they may wait for the initial euphoria to subside before buying.

"Anthropic is a one-trick pony. People compare it with Amazon because even Amazon lost money for several years, but Anthropic won't have that luxury," said Bill Gunderson, partner at GCG Advisory Partners.

"They've got to get to profitability soon."

Anthropic has nearly $900 billion in computing commitments with partners including Amazon and Alphabet's Google, underscoring how its rapid growth hinges on securing vast amounts of future computing capacity, some of which relies on financing beyond the company's control.

Investors will be watching Anthropic's debut and subsequent trading closely, with analysts expecting the stock to emerge as a proxy for the broader AI trade.

The company will also need to balance growth with calls to slow the development of advanced AI models. Anthropic warned in its IPO prospectus that AI could behave unpredictably and advance faster than oversight mechanisms.

(Reporting by Niket Nishant, Manya Saini in Bengaluru and Echo Wang in New York; Additional reporting by Chibuike Oguh; Editing by Christian Plumb and Arun Koyyur)

data.title: OCLC and Ecole Solutions partner to bring EZproxy services to libraries across India
data.description:
Ecole Solutions is now OCLC's distributor for hosted EZproxy and EZproxy
Analytics, providing local sales, training, and support for Indian institutions

DUBLIN, Ohio and BANGALORE, India, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- OCLC and Ecole Solutions, the Bangalore-based provider of technology solutions for libraries and academic institutions, today announced a distribution partnership to make OCLC's hosted EZproxy and EZproxy Analytics available to academic and research libraries in India.

OCLC and Ecole Solutions are partnering to make OCLC's EZproxy available to academic and research libraries in India

Ecole Solutions will market and sell both services and provide local customer support, including implementation, training, and technical assistance. The distribution agreement covers much of the Indian subcontinent, including India, Bangladesh, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Bhutan.

Designed around user privacy, EZproxy simply and securely connects students and researchers to electronic journal articles and other e-resources in a library's collection. Hosted EZproxy is OCLC's fully managed e-resource access and authentication service. It enables libraries to provide authorized users with access to licensed electronic resources using their existing institutional sign-on credentials. EZproxy Analytics complements COUNTER reporting by using powerful data exploration and visualization tools across EZproxy log files to make it easier to curate e-resources and prove their value.

"We're delighted to welcome Ecole Solutions as our partner in India," said Eric van Lubeek, Managing Director, OCLC EMEA/Asia Pacific. "Ecole Solutions' local knowledge and technical expertise will help libraries quickly implement and realize the benefits of EZproxy services. This partnership reflects our long-term commitment to supporting the Indian library community."

India's One Nation One Subscription (ONOS) initiative expands access to scholarly research publications across the country. At the same time, libraries continue to invest in databases, e-books, and other digital resources and need reliable information to assess their use and value.

"EZproxy works with virtually any publisher and alongside the national federations and institutional logins libraries already use, giving researchers one way into their collection, from anywhere," said L. S. Venkatesh, Director, Ecole Solutions. "Librarians gain the usage evidence they need for collection decisions and quality reviews. OCLC hosts the service, and our team provides local support."

OCLC and Ecole Solutions leaders will introduce the new partnership and meet with library leaders at the PLANNER 2026 Convention in Guwahati, India, 25-27 November.

Libraries in India interested in learning more can visit https://www.ecoleglobal.com/.

More about EZproxy is on the OCLC website.

About Ecole Solutions

Ecole Solutions is an India-based technology services provider specializing in digital transformation for educational institutions. It delivers advanced plagiarism and AI-detection software, alongside e-learning and campus management solutions. These tools empower universities nationwide to enforce strict academic integrity and optimize operations.

About OCLC

OCLC is a nonprofit global library organization that provides shared technology services, original research, and community programs so that libraries can better fuel learning, research, and innovation. Through OCLC, member libraries cooperatively produce and maintain WorldCat, the most comprehensive global network of data about library collections and services. Libraries gain efficiencies through OCLC's WorldShare, a complete set of library management applications and services built on an open, cloud-based platform. It is through collaboration and sharing of the world's collected knowledge that libraries can help people find answers they need to solve problems. Together as OCLC, member libraries, staff, and partners make breakthroughs possible.

data.title: Democratic lawmakers probe DOJ filing in OpenAI copyright case
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 19 (Reuters) - A group of Democratic members of the US Congress sent a letter to the US Department of Justice on Thursday demanding answers on why it intervened on behalf of OpenAI in a landmark copyright dispute with news outlets including the New York Times ( NYT ).

The 12 representatives, led by Chellie Pingree of Maine, Becca Balint of Vermont and Deborah Ross of North Carolina, accused DOJ of supporting OpenAI in the case without first consulting the federal government's intellectual property agencies, the US Copyright Office and US Patent and Trademark Office.

The lawmakers requested more information about any "external companies and organizations" that may have influenced DOJ's filing.

The representatives wrote that the DOJ's decision to forgo consultation with the USPTO and Copyright Office raised "serious questions about potential bias," citing Axios reporting that the agencies were surprised by the department's filing.

Spokespeople for DOJ, the US Copyright Office, USPTO and OpenAI did not immediately respond to requests for comment on the letter. A New York Times spokesperson declined to comment.

The Times' lawsuit, first filed in 2023, accuses ​OpenAI and its largest financial ​backer, Microsoft ( MSFT ), of using ⁠millions of newspaper articles without permission to train OpenAI's ChatGPT.

The case is one of the most prominent of the dozens of high-stakes lawsuits brought by copyright holders against tech companies such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta ​Platforms for what they call the misuse of their material to train AI systems.

The ​pending cases will ⁠likely turn on whether AI systems make fair use of copyrighted material by using it to create new, transformative content. OpenAI has told the court that the use of copyrighted work for AI training is "among ​the most transformative many of us ​will see in our lifetimes," while the Times has argued that OpenAI exploits its work to create similar competing content.

DOJ filed a brief in support of OpenAI in September arguing that AI training is generally fair use.

The brief marked the first time that the US government has weighed in on an AI-training copyright case. The lawmakers noted in the letter that the Trump administration has previously said that the issues should be left to the courts.

A separate group of Democratic representatives from the House Judiciary Committee criticized DOJ's filing in a court brief in October, arguing that DOJ "injected its views in this case in a manner that runs contrary to its standard practice" without input from "the federal bodies that possess actual expertise in the subject at hand."

data.title: Bank of America banker Stewart Barry to join Allen & Company, sources say
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov 19 (Reuters) - Bank of America's ( BAC ) Stewart Barry, vice chairman of global technology investment banking, is leaving the lender to join boutique investment bank Allen & Company, according to people familiar with the matter.

Barry, who is based in the San Francisco Bay Area, will join Allen & Company as a senior banker on the West Coast, the people said.

He has been with Bank of America ( BAC ) since 2014 and most recently served as global head of internet, focusing on large-cap internet companies.

He is expected to start at Allen & Co after his garden leave, the sources said.

A spokesperson for Bank of America ( BAC ) declined to comment. Allen & Company did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Allen & Company, the closely held New York-based investment bank, is known for advising technology and media companies and for hosting its annual Sun Valley conference, which attracts many of the industry's top executives, investors and dealmakers.

Barry's departure comes as Bank of America ( BAC ) has lost several other prominent dealmakers over the past year, including in the tech group, such as David Fishman and Ed Liu.

The firm has also hired close to 50 managing directors globally this year, according to one of the people. This week Reuters reported that Bank of America ( BAC ) has hired Francis ​Stapleton from Evercore to lead its global activism and raid defense practice. 

(Reporting by Milana Vinn in New York; editing by Colin Barr and Chizu Nomiyama )

data.title: US STOCKS-Wall St slides as Anthropic's debut fails to revive AI trade optimism
data.description:
* Indexes down: Dow 1.6%, S&P 500 1.29%, Nasdaq 1.29%

* Anthropic briefly hits $2 trillion in market value

* Walmart ( WMT ) down after forecasting annual sales below estimates

* Cybersecurity firms up after Palo Alto Networks ( PANW ) lifts FY27 forecast

(Updates prices throughout)

By Ragini Mathur, Utkarsh Hathi and Medha Singh

Nov 19 (Reuters) - US stock indexes tumbled on Thursday after Anthropic's blockbuster market debut failed to ease concerns about the AI trade, triggering a broader market selloff.

Shares of the AI lab briefly soared past $2 trillion in market valuation, but pared gains and was last trading up 15% around $95.50.

The company priced its upsized offering at $83 per share on Wednesday, above its marketed range of $70 to $78, raising $81 billion in the largest listing on record.

"It has failed to rekindle enthusiasm for tech stocks," said Joe Maher, market economist at Capital Economics, London. "We wouldn't read too much into the expected initial 'pop' in Anthropic's share price as a stock's early trading tends to be noisy."

The listing follows weeks of selling in chipmakers and cloud companies as investors fretted over stretched valuations, heavy spending on AI infrastructure and the fallout from the abrupt exit of Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang.

Amazon ( AMZN ) fell 2.7% while Alphabet ticked down 0.6%. Both are among the biggest investors in the AI lab.

"It's difficult to draw conclusions from the first day of trading. I'd rather step back, let the dust settle and watch how the stock behaves over the next several sessions before making any judgment about its fair value," Ben Barringer, head of technology research at Quilter Cheviot.

Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) shares tumbled 9.2% after investigative outlet Hunterbrook said its affiliated fund, Hunterbrook Capital, had taken a short position in the chipmaker.

Most tech stocks were lower. Nvidia ( NVDA ) declined 1.2% after five straight sessions of losses as its upbeat revenue forecast on Tuesday did little to lift sentiment.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dipped 1%.

Neocloud firms CoreWeave ( CRWV ) and Nebius slipped 3.5% and 6%, respectively.

The broader technology sector was down 1%.

All major S&P 500 sectors slid into negative territory, led by 1.8% declines each in healthcare and consumer staples.

At 01:31 p.m. ET the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 801.12 points, or 1.60%, to 49,397.05, the S&P 500 lost 93.31 points, or 1.29%, to 7,230.32 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 316.45 points, or 1.29%, to 24,113.44.

Data on Thursday showed the number of Americans filing new claims for unemployment benefits increased slightly last week, consistent with a stable labor market.

On Wednesday, hawkish minutes from the US Federal Reserve's latest meeting also weighed on sentiment.

Nearly all Fed officials saw a need for more rate increases if the economy performed as projected, according to the minutes from the central bank's October policy meeting, while a few warned that inflation could be stickier than anticipated and require tighter policy.

Traders are pricing in a near-certainty of a 25-basis-point hike at the Fed's December meeting and about a 6% chance of a 50-basis-point move, according to LSEG data.

Among other movers, Palo Alto Networks ( PANW ) shares jumped 5.6% after the cybersecurity firm raised its 2027 revenue forecast, helping drive gains of 3% to 5% in peers CrowdStrike ( CRWD ) , Okta ( OKTA ) and Zscaler ( ZS ).

Walmart ( WMT ) was down 1% after the retail giant forecast annual sales below estimates.

Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 3.63-to-1 ratio on the NYSE, and by a 2.59-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq. The S&P 500 posted one new 52-week high and 16 new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 25 new highs and 417 new lows.

data.title: Exclusive-US should not certify Chinese aircraft, restrict investments in China's aerospace sector, lawmakers say
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 19 (Reuters) - The US government should refuse to certify Chinese-made airplanes and pull taxpayer contracts from American defense contractors including Airbus if they do not halt investments in China's aerospace industrial base, a congressional report seen by Reuters said.

The House Select Committee on China in a report said Washington should toughen export controls and restrict investments in China's aerospace sector.

"The broader system allowed commercial aerospace engagement that could strengthen firms connected to the PRC's military industrial base without triggering the safeguards designed to protect sensitive technology," the report said following a year-long investigation.

Airbus did not immediately comment.

The report said the Federal Aviation Administration should not allow Chinese-manufactured aircraft to fly in the United States, noting that China has never released its report into the 2022 crash of a China Eastern Airlines Boeing aircraft and citing subsidies that China has given to state-owned Chinese airplane maker COMAC and AVIC. 

The Treasury Department should restrict outbound investment into China's aerospace sector and urge allies to follow suit and subject the purchase of US aerospace companies by French firms to heightened scrutiny until they unwind ties to China's "Civil-Military Ecosystem."

The report said through joint ventures, co-development agreements, and other commercial relationships "American and other Western companies transferred technology, know-how, and industrial capacity" on aerospace that ultimately benefited the Chinese military.

(Reporting by David Shepardson; Editing by Chizu Nomiyama )

data.title: Shufti Launches Glocal Trust OS, Connecting Business-Wide Information with User Risk Signals for Context-Aware Decisions
